exits.label: ◂ back from the Wall's edge, to the Unspooling

npcs.name: Rue
npcs.title: a soul at the Wall's edge, hearing it sing their name
npcs.hail: *(A soul stands too close to the Wall — closer than any soul should choose to — swaying very slightly, the way a person sways to music only they can hear. Their eyes are half-shut and wet, and their face holds two things at once that should not fit together: terror, and something perilously close to longing. When your cold reaches them they flinch, and grab your arm with a drowning grip, and the words come out of them fast and low, as if they have to say them before something interrupts.)* …*(barely, urgent)* …*(you hear it? tell me you don't hear it. — no. no, better you* don't *—)* …*(they haul their gaze from the Wall to your face with visible effort)* …it's — it's *singing*, cold one. the *Wall.* it's been getting *louder* for — i don't know how long, time's *wrong* this close — and it's singing *my* — it *knows* my *name*, it's singing it *soft*, like a — like a *lullaby*, like something that *loves* me, and it *wants* me to *walk* *in*, and the *worst* — *(their grip tightens)* …the *worst* part …is how *much* i *want* to.

variants.text: *(Their wet, half-shut eyes find yours — and go wide, because they see it in you too.)* …*(a whisper of pure dread)* …*you* *hear* it. …*(not a question)* …*don't* you. …*(they don't let go of your arm; if anything they hold on harder, two drowning souls in the same water)* …i can *see* it on you, cold one — the way your *head* just *tilted*, just a *fraction*, toward the — *(they can't say* Wall*)* …*oh* *gods.* *you're* *further* than *me.* the *cold's* got you and the *song* is *reaching* for you *same* as *me* and you didn't even — you've been *hearing* it so *long* you stopped *noticing.* …*(fierce, terrified, and somehow now trying to save* you*)* …then *HELP* me, cold one, *quick*, before it *takes* us *both* — because if a soul who *walks* *out* of the *dark* can *hear* it *singing* …then *none* of us …*none* of us are *safe.*

*(They keep hold of your arm, swaying, fighting to stay turned toward you and not the Wall, and the effort of it is a thing you can see costing them.)* …*(low, fast)* …*talk* to me. *keep* me *talking*, cold one, *please* — as long as i'm *talking* to *you* i'm not — *(their gaze drifts Wall-ward; they wrench it back)* …*sorry.* *sorry.* it — it *pulls.* every time i *stop*, it — the *song* gets *into* the *quiet* and *fills* it. …*(a wet, frightened laugh)* …i came *close* to *look.* that's *all.* just to *see* the *thing* everyone's so *afraid* of. …and it started — it started *singing*, so *soft*, and it *knew* my *NAME*, and now i — *(the terror and the longing war in their face)* …now i can't — cold one, i can't *remember* …*why* i'm supposed to *want* to *stay.* …*help* me *remember.* …*quick.* …while i still *want* you to.

nodes.speaker: Rue
nodes.text: *(They talk fast, holding onto the sound of their own voice like a rope, and you begin — faintly, at the edge of your dead-touched hearing — to catch it too: a melody with no source, unbearably gentle, threaded through with a name that is almost, almost yours.)* …*here's* what it *sings*, cold one, and *this* is the *trap* of it — it doesn't sing *oblivion.* it doesn't promise *nothing.* …*(their voice drops, seduced despite themselves)* …it promises *rest.* it says: *you're* so *TIRED.* you've *carried* so *much*, for so *long*, and it *hurts*, and it doesn't have to. …*walk* *in*, and you can *set* it *ALL* *down* — every *grief*, every *cold* *hour*, every *name* that *weighs* on you — and it will be *warm*, and it will be *quiet*, and you will *never* have to *hold* *anything* *again.* …*(a tear tracks down)* …*that's* the *song*, cold one. it's not *death.* it's *permission* to *stop.* …and i am *so* — *(they shudder)* …i am *so* *tired.* …*(their gaze slides Wall-ward and holds there this time, longer)* …*tell* me *why* …*'tired'* …isn't a *good* enough *reason* …to *walk* *in.*

choices.text: *(read the soul the song is taking — fast, find the anchor, the one thing that could hold them)* "Look at me, Rue — my eyes, not the Wall. Let me look at you. I need to find the thing that keeps you here, and I need to find it fast."

*(the one who walks both ways — you can go a little into the song and pull them back, but you'll hear it too)* "Hold onto me, Rue. I'm the one soul who walks into the dark and comes back out — which means I can walk a few steps into that song and drag you back by the collar. It'll cost me. I'll hear it too, and it'll follow me down the road. But I'd rather carry the song a while than let it carry you. Hold on."

"Tired isn't nothing, Rue — you've earned the wanting. But listen to the trick in it: the song offers to end your grief by ending *you.* That's not rest. That's the Wall dressing up your exhaustion as a choice. You can set the weight down without setting down your *self.* Stay, and I'll show you how."

*(anchor them — you found what holds them; name it, hard, and pull)* "Rue. Stop. Listen to me and not to it. You told me — you have a REASON, one you're letting the song sing over. I'm going to say it back to you, loud, until it's louder than the Wall. Hold onto it. Hold onto ME."
"...I can't stay, Rue. I have to — there are others." *(you make yourself let go of their arm)*

nodes.speaker: Rue
nodes.text: *(You seize their face and make them hold your gaze, and your sense drives in fast — there's no time for the slow careful read, the song is a rising tide and you have moments — and you find, under the seduction, the one thing the Wall's lullaby is singing over.)* *(And it is not grand. It is small, and specific, and alive, and it is exactly the kind of thing the song works hardest to drown, because small living things are heavier anchors than any grand one. Your sense finds it: a person. Someone Rue loves who is not dead yet — still living, up in the world — someone Rue was, in life, the steady one for, the one who showed up, the one who could be counted on. And your sense reads what the song is doing to that: it is singing 'they'll be fine without you, they've grieved you already, your staying changes nothing, set them down with everything else' — and it is lying, the specific lie the Wall tells every soul it wants, that they are not needed, that their staying is a weight and not a gift. And your sense reads the truth that could anchor them, if you can make it louder than the music: that Rue is not tired of *living*, or of loving, or of that person — Rue is tired of *grief*, which is a different thing, and the song has deliberately blurred them, has made 'I can't carry this pain' sound like 'I don't want to be here,' when they are opposites. The person up in the world is not a weight Rue is desperate to set down. The person is the reason Rue came close to the Wall to look and has not yet walked in. Name the person. Make Rue hear their name over the song. That is the rope.)*

nodes.speaker: Rue
nodes.text: *(Your words reach them — you see them land — but the song is louder now, and reason is a thin thread against it, and their gaze keeps sliding.)* …*'end* your *grief* by *ending* *you.'* …*(they nod, slow, drugged)* …*yes.* …that's — i *know* that's the *trick*, cold one, i'm not a *fool*, i can *hear* the *trick* in it — …*(and then, terribly)* …but *knowing* it's a *trick* …doesn't make it *stop* *working.* …that's the *horror* of a *good* *lie*, isn't it. you can *see* the *hook* and *want* it *anyway.* …*(they sway toward the Wall)* …you say i can set the *weight* down without setting down my — but i've *tried*, cold one, i've — the *weight* IS me, now, i can't *tell* where the *grief* *ends* and *i* *begin* anymore, and the *song* says it can *cut* that *knot* and i — …*(they wrench back to you, desperate)* …*give* me something *SOLID*, cold one. not an *argument.* the *song* out-*argues* *everything.* give me something to *HOLD.* …*(this is the moment, and it is slipping)*

nodes.speaker: Rue
nodes.text: *(You take hold of them and you do the thing only a Returned can: you turn, deliberately, toward the Wall, and you let the song in — and it is worse than you imagined, and better, which is why it's dangerous. It is warm. It is a hand smoothing your hair. It sings your name, and it says* you can stop now*, and every cold exhausted stacked-up winter in you leans toward it like a plant toward light. And for one endless moment you understand exactly why souls walk in — not despair, never despair, but relief, the sweetest note there is — and you take one step, and another, into the song, right to the edge of yourself, and you get your arm around Rue where they've drifted, and you hold on, and you turn — against the pull, against the warmth, against the permission to finally set it ALL down — and you drag the both of you back out.)* …*(you come back to yourself at the same instant Rue does, both of you gasping on the cold road, the song howling behind you and then, slowly, receding)* …*(Rue clings to you, weeping, alive)* …you — you *WALKED* into it. *for* me. …*(they can't stop shaking)* …*nobody* — you *heard* it, cold one, i *saw* your *face*, you *heard* how *SWEET* it — and you *turned* *AROUND* *anyway.* …*(and you did, and it followed you out; you can feel it now, a new low note under everything, a coldness that wasn't there before, the song's price, and you will carry it)* …*(Rue grips your hands)* …*don't* — cold one, *don't* you *walk* *back* in *later*, when i'm not — *promise* me. …you *spent* something *precious* to *pull* me *out.* …*don't* let it *turn* out …you *left* it *IN* *there.*

nodes.speaker: Rue
nodes.text: *(You say the name — the living person, the reason, the small heavy anchor — and you say it loud, and again, and again, over the song, refusing to let the melody have the quiet: their name, their face, the thing Rue is the steady one for.)* …*(Rue's swaying stops)* …*(their gaze, which has been sliding Wall-ward this whole time, snaps to your face and stays)* …*(you say it once more)* …*(and something in them catches, like a hook finding purchase, and the drowning grip on your arm becomes a holding-on instead)* …*(they say the name back to you, in a broken whisper, and then again, stronger, and each time they say it the song loses a little of its hold, because a name spoken in love is the one sound the Wall cannot sing over)* …*they're* — *(they gasp)* …*they're* *not* *fine* *without* me. the *song* *said* — it *kept* *saying* they'd — but they're *NOT*, they *need* — *(they're weeping now, but it's the right kind, the kind that pulls you back into the world)* …*i* *forgot.* the song made me *FORGET* i was still — that i still *matter* to someone *breathing.* …*(they turn their back on the Wall, fully, for the first time)* …*i'm* *tired*, cold one. i'm *still* so *tired.* …but *tired* isn't the same as *done.* …you just — you *shouted* the *difference* at me …*until* i could *hear* it. …*(they hold on)* …*don't* let *go* yet. …the *song's* still *there.* …but *your* *voice* …is *louder* …*now.*

nodes.speaker: Rue
nodes.text: *(You find not just the name but the whole living weight of it — the person, and the specific way Rue matters to them, and you don't just shout it, you make Rue *feel* it — and the anchor doesn't just catch, it *holds*, and holds so hard that the song, for the first time, breaks.)* …*(Rue goes rigid, then sags, then stands — really stands, on their own feet, turned wholly away from the Wall)* …*(the song is still there, you can both hear it, but it has stopped sounding like a lullaby and started sounding like what it is: a hungry thing, wheedling, and now that Rue can hear the hunger under the sweetness, it has lost)* …*it* was *LYING.* …*(they say it with the fury of the newly-freed)* …the whole — '*you're* not *needed*, *set* it *down*, they've *grieved* you already' — it was a *LIE*, cold one, and i *believed* it because i was too *tired* to *check.* …*(they take your hands, fierce and awake)* …*here's* what i'm going to *DO* about the *tired.* i'm going to go back down the road, and i'm going to find the *other* souls standing too *close*, *swaying*, *listening* — and i'm going to do to *them* what you just did to *me.* i'm going to *stand* between them and the *song* and *shout* the *name* of *whatever* they *love* until they can *hear* it *over* the music. …*(a shaking, ferocious smile)* …the Wall *sings* one soul at a *time* …because it *has* to *isolate* them to *win.* …*(fierce)* …so we *stop* *standing* at the *edge* *ALONE.* …you didn't just *pull* me *back*, cold one. …you *taught* me the *counter*-*song.* …*it's* just *someone's* *NAME.* …*said* *loud.* …*by* *someone* who *stayed.*

nodes.speaker: Rue
nodes.text: *(You reach for the anchor but your voice shakes, or comes a half-beat late, and the song surges into the gap — and you feel Rue slip, their weight shifting Wall-ward, the drowning grip on your arm loosening toward letting-go.)* …*(dreamy, drifting)* …*it's* …*alright*, cold one. …*(the terror is going out of their face, which is the worst sign there is)* …you *tried.* …that was — that was *kind* of you, to *try* … …*(their eyes are on the Wall now, and soft)* …but it's *so* *warm*, and i'm *so* *tired*, and the *name* you're — *whose* *name*? …i can't — it's *going*, it's all *going*, and it doesn't *hurt* …*(they take a step)* …*(and you have one more chance, and you know it, and everything depends on the next thing you do)* …*(grab them. now. try again. LOUDER. — the choice is a blade's edge and the song is winning)*

nodes.speaker: Rue
nodes.text: *(You do not argue and you do not reason — the time for that is gone. You grab Rue by both shoulders and you haul them bodily around to face you, breaking their line to the Wall, and you put your cold forehead against theirs so the only thing they can see is your face and the only thing they can hear, if you make it loud enough, is you — and you say the name. Not clever. Not gentle. Just the name of the person they love, roared into the half-inch between you, again and again, a blunt instrument against a beautiful song.)* …*(Rue's next step doesn't land)* …*(they blink)* …*(the name gets through — barely, on the third roar, or the fourth — and their eyes focus, and fill, and they grab you back)* …*(gasping, hauled back from the very lip of it)* …*that* — *that* *name* — …*(they're shaking so hard they can barely stand)* …*gods*, i almost — i had my *foot* — …*(they cling to you, and the song, cheated, recedes, sullen)* …*don't* let *go.* …*not* *yet.* …*(a broken whisper)* …*that* was *closer* than — you nearly *lost* me, cold one. …a *half*-*step* *later* and i'd have been — …*(they can't say it)* …*thank* you for *shouting.* …*thank* you for not — for not *reasoning* with a *drowning* *soul.* …you just …*grabbed* me. …*that's* the *only* thing …that *works* …this *close* …to the *edge.*

nodes.speaker: the Wall's song
nodes.text: *(You reach for the anchor — and you get it wrong. The name comes out uncertain, or you fumble for it a beat too long, and the song pours into that beat like water into a broken hull, and you feel it happen: Rue's grip on your arm goes slack, and their face smooths into something terribly, finally peaceful, and they turn away from you toward the Wall with the ease of a sleeper turning over.)* …*(you lunge — too late — your hand closes on cold air where their sleeve was)* …*(Rue takes one step, and then another, unhurried, unafraid, radiant with relief, walking into the song that knows their name)* …*(they do not look back; the song does not permit looking back; that is part of its mercy and its horror)* …*(and at the Wall's grey edge they simply … thin, and blur, and are gone, set down at last, every weight and every grief and every reason, and the singing swells for a moment in something like satisfaction, and then quiets, and there is only the cold road, and the empty place where a soul stood, and you, holding nothing.)* …*(the song, receding, brushes once against you — soft, patient, knowing — as if to say: you hear me too, cold one. and there is no rush. i will still be here … when you are tired enough.)* …*(you carry that out with you. you will not forget the sound of it, or the empty place, or how gentle it was. some souls the road does not let you save. it only lets you witness the cost of being a half-beat too slow.)*

nodes.speaker: Rue
nodes.text: *(You make yourself let go of their arm — and the instant your cold leaves their skin, you see the song reclaim the space you were holding, see their gaze drift back Wall-ward, unopposed.)* …*(distantly, already half-gone from you)* …*oh.* …*yes.* …*go* on, then, cold one. …*(they're swaying again)* …*others.* *of* *course.* there are *always* *others* who — …*(the terror doesn't return; the song has the quiet now)* …*(and as you turn to go, the last clear thing they say reaches you, and it is not for you, it is for the music)* …*(soft) …coming. …i'm coming. just … let me watch them go first.* …*(you do not know, walking away, whether they mean the Returned who is leaving, or whether they have already begun to walk the other way. the not-knowing is its own weight. you should not have let go of the arm. some part of you knows that, and will keep knowing it, a long way down the road.)*
